newsitem.title: USA: IBM Vermont plant closed after bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: IBM Vermont plant closed after bomb threat.

text.p: Police evacuated an IBM semiconductor plant and were searching for a bomb Wednesday after an unidentified male telephoned a threat to local police.
"We've evacuated the plant and nobody's in there," said Essex Junction police dispatcher Wendy Fuller. "But all the surrounding schools and the homes are still occupied."
Fuller said a decision on whether to evacuate surrounding buildings will be made later.
The plant employs as many as 7,000 workers and operates 24 hours, Fuller said. Officials with IBM were not immediately available to comment.

Burlington Free Press reported Wednesday the plant manufactures microprocessors which run personal computers, logic computer chips used in everything from cars to home appliances, and other semiconductor products.
An IBM spokesman told the newspaper that shutting the plant will cost the company $1 million a day.
Essex Junction police received the phone call early on Tuesday and decided to evacuate the plant around 1700 EST, Fuller said.
Bomb-sniffing dogs from Connecticut and Vermont were called in and were searching for a bomb on Wednesday, she said.
